_note: One case per rule in src/manifest.js, which is the manifest validator specified in docs/contracts/world-loader.md section 6. Completeness rule: every id in MANIFEST_RULES must appear as the `rule` of at least one case here, and every case must reproduce its `expect` list exactly. Adding a rule without a case turns check-fixture red, which is the point. Same conventions as fixtures/hostile/cases.json: `patch` is deep-merged over the named world's real manifest and `null` deletes a key. `templatePatch` is a list of [find, replace] pairs applied to a named template IN MEMORY, for the rules that read the declared templates. `expect` is the DELTA from the unpatched world's own report, so the visual novel's three standing F2 warnings do not have to be repeated in every case that uses it.
_s23: Scenario S23 in the contract patches an extra key into cartoon's `mascot` asset set and expects E1. It does not fire, and the contract is out of date rather than the code: cartoon declares `values` explicitly, so `declaredAssets` enumerates the declared list and never reaches the new key. The C5 proper-subset warning is what that manifest actually earns. E1 is covered by S24's cross product instead, which is the more interesting half anyway — half a cross product is a world that breaks only when one character makes one face.
